svg.title: A $24,000 Base Startup Allocation
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-07-startup-capital-buckets; chart type: stacked_comparison; title: A $24,000 Base Startup Allocation; subtitle: Four buckets reconcile to $8,000 lean, $24,000 base, and $45,000 expanded.; chapter number: 4; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: Numeric values encode the $24,000 base startup allocation in USD. Lean and expanded allocations appear in each stage detail and sum independently to the canonical range endpoints. Cash reserves are unspent liquidity, not immediate operating expense; startup outlays are not added again to the annual profit bridge.; caption: Base: $6,000 + $5,000 + $7,000 + $6,000 = $24,000. Lean: $2,000 + $2,000 + $2,500 + $1,500 = $8,000. Expanded: $12,000 + $10,000 + $14,000 + $9,000 = $45,000.; stages: label: Activity and vendor setup; value: $6,000 base; 25.00% of startup cash; numeric value: 6000.0; detail: Lean $2,000; base $6,000; expanded $12,000. Purchase activity-classification work, partner-contract analysis, and required vendor application preparation. The lean version must narrow its permitted launch scope if actual professional fees or registration costs exceed this allocation.; label: Terminal and attribution build; value: $5,000 base; 20.83% of startup cash; numeric value: 5000.0; detail: Lean $2,000; base $5,000; expanded $10,000. Fund initial feed adapters, PostgreSQL event storage, signed webhook verification, subscription billing integration, and stale-feed tests. Start with a small permitted source set rather than assuming universal exchange or sportsbook access.; label: Content and acquisition experiments; value: $7,000 base; 29.17% of startup cash; numeric value: 7000.0; detail: Lean $2,500; base $7,000; expanded $14,000. Build jurisdiction-specific comparison content and run bounded subscription and affiliate acquisition tests. Keep campaign budgets separate by lane, and stop spend when accepted-event economics fail the documented contribution threshold.; label: Settlement and operating reserve; value: $6,000 base; 25.00% of startup cash; numeric value: 6000.0; detail: Lean $1,500; base $6,000; expanded $9,000. Preserve liquidity for settlement delays, refunds, partner disputes, and unexpected setup costs. At the metadata's $1,500-$10,000 monthly outlay range, the base reserve covers 0.6-4.0 months, before considering the higher full Base-Case cost structure.

rect.title: label: Activity and vendor setup; numeric value: 6000.0; value: $6,000 base; 25.00% of startup cash; detail: Lean $2,000; base $6,000; expanded $12,000. Purchase activity-classification work, partner-contract analysis, and required vendor application preparation. The lean version must narrow its permitted launch scope if actual professional fees or registration costs exceed this allocation.

rect.title: label: Terminal and attribution build; numeric value: 5000.0; value: $5,000 base; 20.83% of startup cash; detail: Lean $2,000; base $5,000; expanded $10,000. Fund initial feed adapters, PostgreSQL event storage, signed webhook verification, subscription billing integration, and stale-feed tests. Start with a small permitted source set rather than assuming universal exchange or sportsbook access.

Build jurisdiction-specific comparison content and run bounded subscription and affiliate acquisition tests. Keep campaign budgets separate by lane, and stop spend when accepted-event economics fail the documented contribution threshold.

Preserve liquidity for settlement delays, refunds, partner disputes, and unexpected setup costs. At the metadata's $1,500-$10,000 monthly outlay range, the base reserve covers 0.6-4.0 months, before considering the higher full Base-Case cost structure.
